segments.t: In Mathias's office late at night, Noemie is hard at work solving a complicated shooting schedule. Mathias joins her, and as they examine the script sequences together, personal feelings resurface. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Il faut s'arrêter, Noémie, il est tard.
J'ai pris du retard dans mon travail.
Je voulais m'excuser pour hier.
Ce n'est pas ta faute, Mathias.
La situation est complexe.
J'avais peur que tu sois fâché contre moi.
Désolé de t'avoir mise dans cette situation.
Tu ne peux pas passer la nuit sur ces plannings.
Mais je suis sûre que ça peut marcher.
Ils doivent commencer par la fin du tournage.
Voyons voir, quelle séquence?
La séquence soixante-neuf.
Voilà le résumé de la scène.
Oui, ils peuvent commencer par là.
Tu as fait un travail formidable, Noémie.
Merci, Mathias.
Let's examine how Mathias and Noemie are sharing an intimate moment working late.
Il faut s'arrêter, Noémie, il est tard.
'We must stop, Noemie, it is late.' Saying it is late at night uses 'it is late' for clock time—distinct from 'in delay' when someone arrives late in French.
J'ai pris du retard dans mon travail.
'I got behind in my work.' Literally 'I took some delay', this handy workplace expression is how you say you 'fell behind' on tasks.
Je voulais m'excuser pour hier.
'I wanted to apologize for yesterday.' Softening 'wanted' with the '-ais' past ending sounds gentler and more polite when apologizing—literally 'excuse myself'—in French.
Ce n'est pas ta faute, Mathias.
'It is not your fault, Mathias.' Slipping back to casual 'your' late at night reveals their closeness, in a reassuring sentence you'll hear word-for-word like English.
La situation est complexe.
'The situation is complex.' Nearly letter-for-letter cognates with English, 'the situation' keeps its article and shifts stress to the final syllable in French.
J'avais peur que tu sois fâché contre moi.
'I was afraid you were angry with me.' Notice French says 'angry against me' rather than 'angry with me', using an emotion form on 'be' after 'afraid that'.
Désolé de t'avoir mise dans cette situation.
'Sorry for having put you in this situation.' Because 'you'—referring to Noemie—comes ahead of 'having put', 'put' adds a pronounced '-e' at the end in French.
Tu ne peux pas passer la nuit sur ces plannings.
'You cannot spend the night on these schedules.' Spending time uses 'pass the night' rather than 'spend' in French, while 'spend' itself is reserved for money.
Mais je suis sûre que ça peut marcher.
'But I am sure that it can work.' Written with a silent '-e' on 'sure' for Noemie, the sentence closes with 'can walk'—the everyday idiom meaning 'can work out'.
Ils doivent commencer par la fin du tournage.
'They must start with the end of the shoot.' Starting with a particular step pairs 'begin' with 'by' rather than 'with' in French—literally 'begin by the end'.
Voyons voir, quelle séquence?
'Let us see, which sequence?' Literally 'let us see to-see', doubling the 'see' idea creates a cozy, thoughtful filler expression for 'let's have a look'.
La séquence soixante-neuf.
'Sequence sixty-nine.' Counting through the sixties stays straightforward—'sixty-nine'—right before counting switches to 'sixty-ten' at seventy in French!
Voilà le résumé de la scène.
'Here is the summary of the scene.' Watch the false friend: borrowed into English for a CV, that term simply means a 'summary' or 'synopsis' in French.
Oui, ils peuvent commencer par là.
'Yes, they can start there.' Closing with 'by there' echoes 'start by' from earlier, giving a neat two-word chunk meaning 'start from that point' in French.
Tu as fait un travail formidable, Noémie.
'You did a wonderful job, Noemie.' Saying 'you made a wonderful work' is the idiomatic way to praise someone for 'doing a terrific job' in French.
Merci, Mathias.

'Thank you, Mathias.' Quiet and direct, pairing 'thanks' with his first name needs no extra words to close the late-night scene in French. Now let's listen to the whole discussion again without stopping.
Il faut s'arrêter, Noémie, il est tard.
J'ai pris du retard dans mon travail.
Je voulais m'excuser pour hier.
Ce n'est pas ta faute, Mathias.
La situation est complexe.
J'avais peur que tu sois fâché contre moi.
Désolé de t'avoir mise dans cette situation.
Tu ne peux pas passer la nuit sur ces plannings.
Mais je suis sûre que ça peut marcher.
Ils doivent commencer par la fin du tournage.
Voyons voir, quelle séquence?
La séquence soixante-neuf.
Voilà le résumé de la scène.
Oui, ils peuvent commencer par là.
Tu as fait un travail formidable, Noémie.
Merci, Mathias.
Working side by side in the quiet office, Mathias and Noemie find a solution to the schedule crisis. Their professional collaboration rekindles their deep personal connection. See you next time!
Bonne nuit, Noémie.
